description: We are a passionate and ambitious team of Computer Science students interested in AI, Data Science, programming, and space exploration. We bring together creativity, technical skills, teamwork, and a strong willingness to learn. Our goal is to collaborate, think outside the box, and develop innovative solutions to real-world challenges using technology and scientific thinking. summary:
Flame in Freefall is an interactive dashboard and evidence-driven mission intelligence platform built using open-access NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion datasets. Developed with Python, Streamlit, Plotly, Microsoft Power BI, and a Groq-powered multi-agent Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) assistant, it transforms complex experimental records into accessible, actionable insights.

The dashboard enables users to explore and cross-filter combustion experiments from ACME, BASS-II, SAFFIRE, and related NASA studies by mission scenario, fire-safety domain, flight platform, cabin atmosphere, and sensor data, including electric-field voltage, ion current, fuel flow, and thermocouple readings. Its AI assistant answers research and safety questions using retrieved NASA PSI records and dashboard data, with traceable evidence and an offline fallback. Users can also export filtered findings, risk assessments, and engineering recommendations as Markdown or PDF mission briefs.

Fire behaves differently in microgravity, where reduced buoyancy alters flame spread, heat transfer, and detection. Oxygen-enriched habitats may introduce additional risks. By connecting NASA research with interactive visualization and transparent, evidence-grounded AI, Flame in Freefall helps researchers and mission planners assess combustion hazards and develop safer fire-detection, prevention, and suppression strategies for future space missions. It avoids manual raw-log reviews.
details: 1. Overview & What the Project DoesFlame in Freefall is an end-to-end Interactive Dashboard and Evidence-Driven Mission Intelligence Platform built around NASA's open-access Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion repository. The platform bridges raw archival spaceflight fire research with actionable mission-planning intelligence by combining a real-time, cross-filtered visual analytics dashboard with a side-by-side, zero-hallucination AI Engineering Assistant.Through a unified split-screen interface, engineers, researchers, and mission planners can:Explore Mission Profiles & Cabin Atmospheres: Dynamically switch between spaceflight environments—including ISS Microgravity, 1/6g Lunar Habitat (32% $O_2$, 10.2 psi), and Mars Transit—to evaluate how reduced gravity and elevated oxygen concentrations alter flame behavior.Cross-Filter NASA PSI Investigations & Telemetry: Visually slice experimental records across fire domains (Fundamental Combustion Physics, Detection, Suppression, and Prevention), flight platforms, and relevance scores, while inspecting sensor-level telemetry (EfieldVoltage, IonCurrent, MFCA3FuelFlow, and multi-channel thermocouples TCA, TCB, TCBurner, TCC, Ch21) from benchmark NASA experiments such as ACME (PSI-22), BASS-II (PSI-25), SAFFIRE-II/III (PSI-99 / PSI-100), and PSI-60.Query a Dashboard-Aware AI Assistant: Ask technical fire-safety questions in natural language and receive structured, citation-backed engineering answers strictly grounded in verified NASA PSI records and the dashboard's underlying data schema.Export Executive Mission Briefs: Generate and download formatted .pdf and .md technical safety reports summarizing filtered findings, hazard assessments, and sensor/suppression recommendations in one click.2. How It Works (System Architecture)Flame in Freefall operates on a modular four-layer pipeline:Data Ingestion & Normalization Layer: Raw NASA PSI ISA-Tab metadata (s_*.txt, a_*.txt) and experimental telemetry tables (G1_Experiment, K1_Setpoints, Publications, Studies) are parsed, cleaned, and structured into lightweight, high-speed schemas (clean_nasa_psi.json and fire_dashboard_chatbot_ready.json) to eliminate latency and optimize cloud deployment.Interactive Visualization & Cross-Filtering Layer: Built with Streamlit, Plotly, and Microsoft Power BI data modeling, the left-hand workspace renders live KPIs, domain distributions, mission relevance rankings, oxygen-envelope curves, and selected investigation cards. Clicking or filtering any parameter dynamically updates both the visual charts and the active context passed to the AI.Grounded Multi-Agent RAG Intelligence Engine: When a user submits a prompt (or clicks a context-aware suggested prompt), the backend retrieves matching PSI records and Power BI schema definitions, injects them into a strict zero-hallucination system prompt, and queries Groq's low-latency LLM API. A transparent Execution Pipeline Trace displays the exact retrieval and reasoning steps, while a built-in deterministic offline fallback engine guarantees continuous operation even without external API connectivity.Automated Reporting Layer: Using FPDF2, the platform compiles the active mission context, filtered investigation evidence, and AI-synthesized safety protocols into a clean, downloadable PDF engineering brief.3. Project GoalsDemocratize Access to NASA PSI Data: Transform complex, multi-file ISA-Tab archives and raw combustion logs into an intuitive, visual, and conversational experience accessible to researchers, students, and mission designers.Eliminate AI Hallucination in Safety-Critical Domains: Enforce strict retrieval grounding so every technical claim, threshold, or experimental reference is traceable to a verified NASA PSI study.Accelerate Deep-Space Fire Safety Design: Provide rapid comparative analysis across microgravity and partial-gravity ($1/6g$ Lunar, $3/8g$ Martian) exploration atmospheres to inform fire detection, material selection, and suppression strategies.4. Key Benefits & ImpactRapid Evidence Synthesis: Reduces hours of manual literature and dataset cross-referencing into seconds of interactive filtering and targeted Q&A.Unified Analytics & Conversational AI: Unlike standalone dashboards or generic chatbots, the AI assistant is directly aware of the user's active dashboard filters, selected investigation (PSI-ID), and mission atmosphere.High Reliability & Portability: Cloud-hosted with lightweight JSON/CSV data structures and offline deterministic fallback logic, ensuring uninterrupted availability during live mission reviews or field demonstrations.5. Tools, Programming Languages, Hardware & Software UsedProgramming Languages: Python 3, JSON, Markdown, CSS (custom UI theming for Light/Dark modes).Frameworks & Libraries:Streamlit: Interactive web application framework and split-view UI layout.Plotly: Interactive, cross-filtered scientific charts and visual analytics.Pandas & NumPy: Data cleaning, ISA-Tab parsing, and statistical aggregation.Groq Python SDK: Ultra-fast LLM inference for the grounded AI Assistant.FPDF2: Automated generation of downloadable PDF mission safety briefs.Software & Platforms:Microsoft Power BI Desktop: Exploratory data modeling, schema design, and dashboard visual architecture (fire dashboard.pbix).Visual Studio Code (VS Code): Primary development environment.Git & GitHub: Version control and repository management ([https://github.com/omarr70/flame-in-freefall](https://github.com/omarr70/flame-in-freefall)).Streamlit Community Cloud: Live cloud hosting and public deployment ([https://flame-in-freefall.streamlit.app](https://flame-in-freefall.streamlit.app)).Hardware: Standard developer workstations/laptops for data processing, local testing, and cloud deployment (zero specialized local GPU hardware required due to lightweight data architecture and cloud LLM inference).
